rv.q: It’s a succinct, well-told thriller, and a look at how the shadows of racism darkened the life and career of one promising young writer.
The play runs just over an hour, but it is a thrilling and intense 65 minutes.

This is a play not just of African American interest but is truly an American story, told from a perspective that many whites might not have considered: having to do with the racial divide in a city and on a campus where white people and white privilege dominated.

cn.t: Kennedy's examination of Jim Crow-era racism at a northern university proves haunting and historically illuminating, though the mystery-tinged narrative carries a certain fatalism as it depicts segregation's cruel impact on Black students.
